intent: A horizontal rule between two sets of rows in a DropdownMenu.
typical_uses: A break between everyday actions and a destructive one at the end of the menu

dont_use_when.situation: A rule between sections of a page or a card, outside any menu

invariants.text: dropdown-menu.module.css pulls the rule out by the popup's padding on both sides, so it runs edge to edge across the popup, and gives it vertical margin of its own.
dropdown-menu.module.css draws only a horizontal rule; `orientation` changes the announced orientation, not the drawing.
The separator renders with role `separator`, takes no pointer events and is not a row that arrow keys land on.

anti_patterns.dont: Put a separator first or last in the popup, or two in a row
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place separators only between rows; a rule at an edge or doubled draws a break with nothing on one side

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A rule before a destructive action

bad.title: A general Separator used inside the popup
bad.why: The popup accepts DropdownMenuSeparator, whose margins are set for the popup's padding; a general Separator stops short of the popup's edges.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.
